Judgment

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of death of Shivaramu, who is husband of petitioner No.1 and father of petitioners No.2 and 3, in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows :
On 04-04-2021 at about 11.25 a.m., deceased Shivaramu was riding a motorcycle bearing No.KA-42-E-9532 in order to going to his land situated at Thangnayakanahalli, carefully, cautiously and observing all the traffic rules.

At that time one Maruthi Swift car bearing No.KA-02-MG-5688, driven by its driver at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, came from Kanakapura towards V. R.
Doddi side and dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased.
As a result, the deceased fell down on the road along with motorcycle and sustained fracture of right leg, head and other injuries all over the body.

Immediately after accident, he was shifted to Kanakapura Government Hospital, wherein first aid was given and then he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, wherein he took treatment as in-patient for 12 days and undergone surgery and discharged with an advise to take follow up treatment.
After discharge he has taken regular treatment at house, since during that period in Karnataka severe pandemic covid-19 had spread.
On 24-04-2021, the deceased started behaving abnormally.
Hence, the petitioners tried to shift him to Kanakapura Government Hospital, but he died before admitted in the hospital.

The petitioners informed the jurisdictional police as well as Kanakapura Government Chikkathayamma vs Coco Dhfl General Insurance Co. Ltd on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2780275/
2 Hospital to conduct the post-mortem.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But, the doctors did not conduct the post-mortem due to severe Covid-19 pandemic cases were admitted in the hospital.
Earlier to the accident, the deceased was doing agricultural work and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
But, on account of his untimely death petitioners have lost the dependency, love and affection.
The Sathnoor Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their respective counsels and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing No.KA-02-MG-5688 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It has contended that the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

It has contended that, the alleged accident has occurred due to the negligence of the deceased himself, as he was riding his motorcycle on the middle of the road, without looking the oncoming vehicles, suddenly swerved his motorcycle and came in the line of motion of the car and hit to the car.
Further it is contended that, the deceased was not wearing helmet and was not holding driving licence to ride the motorcycle.
The deceased himself is liable for the accident, as such there is no actionable negligence attributed to the driver of car.
It has further contended that, the petitioners No.2 and 3 are major sons of the deceased, they were not depending on the income of the deceased.
It has further contended that, as per charge-sheet the Shivaramu has died due to Covid-19 pandemic, there is no post-mortem conducted, he died after 8 days of discharge from the hospital.
As per wound certificate he has sustained only leg injury, there is no nexus between death and injury, he has died due to covid and not due to injury sustained in the accident.
Further it is contended that, the driver of the offending car was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle, as on the date of accident.
It has denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and relationship of petitioners with the deceased.
Further, it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2 under Section 170 of the Motor Vehicle Act.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition.
5. The respondent No.2 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

He has contended that, he is the RC owner of the vehicle involved in the accident and he has got valid driving licence, registration certificate and insurance policy, valid for the period 06-09- 2020 to 05-09-2021.

He has contended that, at the time of accident the deceased was crossing the road without observing the vehicles coming on his back side, abruptly and suddenly came across the road, without following the traffic rules and led to the alleged incident.
He has not committed any offence as alleged by the police.
Therefore, he is not at all liable to pay any compensation as claimed by the petitioners.

Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and Chikkathayamma vs Coco Dhfl General Insurance Co. Ltd on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2780275/
3 exorbitant.

6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES

1 . Whether the petitioners prove that, deceased Shivaramu succumbed to the injuries sustained in vehicular accident alleged to have occurred on 04-04-2021, at 11:25 a.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing registration No.KA-02-MG-5688 ?

2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
7.
In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 20 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.20.
Further, they have got examined two more witnesses namely Ravi and Dr. Chidanand as P.W.2 and P.W.3 and closed their side.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has examined its official as R.W.1 and got marked 2 documents as Ex.R.1 & 2.
The Respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence on his side.
8. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

9. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Partly Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioners that, on 04-04-2021 at about 11.25 a.m., when the deceased Shivaramu was riding his motorcycle bearing No.KA-42-E- 9532, carefully and observing all the traffic rules

, the offending Maruthi Swift car bearing No.KA-02-MG-5688, driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, came from Kanakapura towards V. R. Doddi side and dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased.
As a result, the deceased fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident the deceased was doing agricultural work and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
But, on account of his untimely death they have lost their dependency, love and affection.
11. In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 has got examined herself as P.W.1 by filing her examination-in- chief affidavit, wherein she has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of her oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 20 documents as Ex.P.1 to 20.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R. and first information statement,

12. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 10, prima-facia it reveals that, on 04-04- 2021 at about 11.25 a.m., when the deceased Shivaramu was riding his motorcycle bearing No.KA-42-E-9532, on the left side of the road, from Thanganayakanahalli towards Chudihalli circle, the offending Maruthi Swift car bearing No.KA-02-MG-5688, driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, came from Kanakapura towards V. R. Doddi side and dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased.
As a result, the deceased fell down on the road and has sustained grievous injuries.

The investigation officer has clearly stated in his final report/charge-sheet, which is marked as Ex.P.10 that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing No.KA-02-MG-5688.
13.

At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, the date, time and place of accident, involvement of car bearing KA-02-MG- 5688 in the alleged accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.1 with respect to said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

But,
the respondent No.1 & 2 have specifically denied that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing Reg. No. KA-02-MG-5688.

Further, they have taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has occurred due to negligence of the deceased himself, as he was riding his motorcycle on the middle of the road, without looking the oncoming vehicles,
suddenly swerved his motorcycle and came in the line of motion of the car and hit to the car.

But,
except the self serving statements of R.W.1, who is the representative/Legal Officer of respondent No.1 insurance company, there is absolutely no other oral or documentary evidence produced by the respondents to establish the said contentions.
The P.W.1 has unequivocally denied all the suggestions made in her cross-examination that, the alleged accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the deceased himself.
Further, the oral evidence of P.W.1 is fully corroborated with the documentary evidence and the evidence of P.W.2, who is the eye-witness to the accident in question.
The P.W.2 has deposed in consonance with the evidence of P.W.1.
He has clearly deposed in his evidence that, on 04-04-2021 at about 11:25 a.m., he was standing near Thanganayakanahalli circle.

At that time, the deceased Shivaramu was riding his motorcycle slowly and cautiously, on the left side of the road, from Thanganayakanahalli towards Chudihalli circle and the offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-02-MG-5688 came from Kanakapura side towards V. R.
Doddi, in high speed and in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased and caused grievous injuries to him.
He has clearly deposed that, the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car and there was no negligence on the part of the deceased.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 & 2 have cross-examined P.W.1 & P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from their mouth which Chikkathayamma vs Coco Dhfl General Insurance Co. Ltd on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2780275/
5 creates doubt on the veracity of their evidence.

sentences.text: There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondents to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners.

14. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on 15 feet wide Kanapura- Venkatarayanadoddi main road, at the distance of 10 feet from the left side of the road, near Thanganayakanahalli village circle, Sathanuru Hobli, Kanakapura taluka, Ramanagar district, in between motorcycle bearing No.KA- 42-E-9532 and car bearing Reg.
No.KA-02-MG-5688.

Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.7,
the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-MG-5688 and there was not negligence on the part of the deceased, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to negligence of the driver of offending car.

As per Ex.P.10 final report/charge-sheet,
the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-02-MG-5688.
Admittedly, the said charge-sheet has not been challenged by the driver or owner of the said car.

Further, there is absolutely no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondents and even nothing has been elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 & P.W.2 to show that, the said accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the deceased himself and there is no negligence on the part of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-02-MG-5688.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the deceased Shivaramu in the said accident.

15. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.5 wound certificate, Ex.P.19 MLC register extract and Ex.P.20 in-patient records, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
He has sustained Type 2 open both bone fracture of right leg.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the above medical records produced by the petitioners are false documents.

In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners, regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-02-MG-5688 and injuries caused to the deceased Shivaramu in the said accident.

16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

18. In the present case, the petitioners are claiming that, the deceased Shivaramu has died due to injuries sustained in the accident in question.
But, except the self serving statements of P.W.1, there is absolutely no evidence on record to show that, the deceased Shivaramu has died due to injuries sustained in the said accident.
It is pertinent to note that, as per the medical records available on record, the deceased Shivaramu has sustained grievous injury only on his right leg i.e. fracture of both bones of right leg.
Except the said injury, the deceased has not sustained any other grievous injury on any of the vital part of his body.

Further it is pertinent to note that, as per Ex.P.20 in-patient record, the deceased has taken treatment at Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma &
Orthopedics Hospital, Bengaluru, from 04-04-2021 to 16-04-2021.

sentences.text: After undergoing treatment for 13 days, the deceased Shivaramu was discharged from the hospital on 16-04-2021 and thereafter he was taking rest at his home.
While taking rest at this home, the said Shivaramu has died on 24-04-2021.

It is clearly stated in the Ex.P.10 final report/charge-sheet that, after discharge from the hospital the deceased Shivaramu was taking rest at his home and on 24-04-2021 at about 10:45 a.m., he died due to Covid-19 pandemic.
Admittedly, the petitioners have not challenged the said final report/charge-sheet.
Further, the petitioners have not produced the post-mortem report to show that, the injured Shivaramu has died due to injuries sustained in the accident in question.
Even nothing with respect to same has been deposed by the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has treated the petitioner with respect to injury sustained to his right leg.
There is absolutely no evidence placed on record to show that, there is nexus in between the injuries sustained to the petitioner in the accident and cause of his death.

19. Therefore, in such circumstances and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioners has successfully proved through cogent and corroborative evidence that, the deceased Shivaramu has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident, occurred on 04-04-2021 at about 11.25 a.m., near Thanganayakanahalli village circle, Sathanuru Hobli,
Kanakapura taluka, Ramanagar district, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing registration No.KA-02-MG-5688.
But, the petitioners have failed to proved that, Shivaramu has died due to the injuries sustained in the said accident.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Partly Affirmative.
20. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue, for the reasons stated therein, this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioners have successfully proved that, the deceased Shivaramu has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident, occurred occurred on 04-04-2021 at about 11.25 a.m.,
near Thanganayakanahalli village circle, Sathanuru Hobli, Kanakapura taluka, Ramanagar district,
due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing registration No.KA-02-MG-5688.

If the deceased Shivaramu had been alive he would have been entitled for pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life,
loss of prospects of marriage etc.

But, unfortunately as he has expired due to Covid-19 pandemic, the issue with regard to assessment and granting compensation under the heads; future loss of earning,
loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc., does not survive for Chikkathayamma vs Coco Dhfl General Insurance Co. Ltd on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2780275/
7 consideration.

sentences.text: Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-02-MG-5688.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-02-MG-5688, the accident in question has taken place.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the said vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.54,593/- from the respondent No.1, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.54,593/- (Rupees fifty four thousand five hundred and ninety three only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioners.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.1 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

The above compensation amount is apportioned as follows:
Petitioner No.1 - Wife - 50% Petitioner No.2 - Son - 25% Petitioner No.3 - Son - 25%
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest awarded to petitioners No.1 to 3 shall be released in their favour, through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of death of Shivaramu, who is husband of petitioner No.1 and father of petitioners No.2 and 3, in a road traffic accident.
The petitioners informed the jurisdictional police as well as Kanakapura Government Chikkathayamma vs Coco Dhfl General Insurance Co. Ltd on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2780275/
2 Hospital to conduct the post-mortem.
The Sathnoor Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing No.KA-02-MG-5688 and its validity as on the date of accident.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
It has contended that the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
18. In the present case, the petitioners are claiming that, the deceased Shivaramu has died due to injuries sustained in the accident in question.
opennyai_summary.issue:
6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES
1 . Whether the petitioners prove that, deceased Shivaramu succumbed to the injuries sustained in vehicular accident alleged to have occurred on 04-04-2021, at 11:25 a.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing registration No.KA-02-MG-5688 ?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-MG-5688 and there was not negligence on the part of the deceased, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to negligence of the driver of offending car.
Further, there is absolutely no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondents and even nothing has been elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 & P.W.2 to show that, the said accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the deceased himself and there is no negligence on the part of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-02-MG-5688.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the deceased Shivaramu in the said accident.
He has sustained Type 2 open both bone fracture of right leg.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the above medical records produced by the petitioners are false documents.
In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners, regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car bearing Reg. No.KA-02-MG-5688 and injuries caused to the deceased Shivaramu in the said accident.
16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone Chikkathayamma vs Coco Dhfl General Insurance Co. Ltd on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2780275/
6 of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt
But, except the self serving statements of P.W.1, there is absolutely no evidence on record to show that, the deceased Shivaramu has died due to injuries sustained in the said accident.
It is pertinent to note that, as per the medical records available on record, the deceased Shivaramu has sustained grievous injury only on his right leg i.e. fracture of both bones of right leg.
Except the said injury, the deceased has not sustained any other grievous injury on any of the vital part of his body.
There is absolutely no evidence placed on record to show that, there is nexus in between the injuries sustained to the petitioner in the accident and cause of his death.
If the deceased Shivaramu had been alive he would have been entitled for pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life,
loss of prospects of marriage etc.
But, unfortunately as he has expired due to Covid-19 pandemic, the issue with regard to assessment and granting compensation under the heads; future loss of earning,
loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc., does not survive for Chikkathayamma vs Coco Dhfl General Insurance Co. Ltd on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2780275/
7 consideration.
In such circumstances, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioners are entitled for the pecuniary damages, such as expenses for medical treatment, attendants and conveyance, due to grievous injuries caused to the deceased in the said accident.

21. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1.

Conveyance expenses 10,000-00 Total Rs. 54,593-00
In all, the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.54,593/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum,
from the date of petition till its realization.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.54,593/- from the respondent No.1, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.54,593/- (Rupees fifty four thousand five hundred and ninety three only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioners.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.1 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
The above compensation amount is apportioned as follows:
Petitioner No.1 - Wife - 50% Petitioner No.2 - Son - 25% Petitioner No.3 - Son - 25%
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest awarded to petitioners No.1 to 3 shall be released in their favour, through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
